activity_context.topic_title: The Image and Rank of a Linear Transformation

feedback.problem: Given the transformation $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x+y+z \\ z+y-x \\ z-2y\end{aligned}],$ find its rank.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, the standard matrix of $T$ is given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Recall that $\text{rank}(T)=\text{dim}(\text{Im}(T))=\text{rank}(T).$ 

So, we need to find the rank of the matrix $T.$ We reduce $T$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, since $T$ has $3$ pivot columns, we have that 

$$
\text{rank}(T)=\text{rank}(T)=3.
$$
